memory.title: Memory
memory.unavailable: The memory settings could not be read. Reopen this screen; if it stays like this, check config.json.
memory.reviewHint: A review pass does not add: it makes things smaller. Below {floor} runs two passes meet, and the second prunes what the first already removed — that needs an explicit confirmation.
memory.reviewConfirm: A cadence of {runs} runs is below the floor of {floor}. Measured on the phone: two consecutive passes took USER.md from 3,524 characters to 1,626 — 31% of it on the second pass alone — and a forced pass removed five real entries: two open questions, a plan, a biographical detail and one insight. Every entry that leaves is archived under memory/archive/ first, so nothing is lost: what it still costs is tokens, on every run, unattended. Set it anyway?
memory.sinceReview: {runs} runs since the last review pass.
memory.stuckRuns: {runs} runs in a row with writes attempted and none landing.
memory.nothingNewRuns: {runs} runs in a row with nothing to consolidate.
memory.budgetsHint: How large each of the three files that go into every prompt may grow. Zero means measure and never refuse. A file at its budget is not a fault, but it is the first thing to check when Dream reports it consolidated nothing.

workers.title: Wiki and projects
workers.unavailable: The periodic worker settings could not be read. Reopen this screen; if it stays like this, check config.json.
workers.gardenerOffHint: Turning it off is not uninstalling it: /gardener inside a project still runs a pass by hand.
workers.gardenerDistance: Gap between two passes on one project (h)
workers.gardenerNumbersHint: A tick that finds no new journal lines spends no tokens, so looking often is cheap: what decides is the silence. The gardener works on cold material — going in while you are talking would promote half of a conversation and rewrite the map while you read it. The gap is the measured degradation of Dream written as a number: a second close pass on one subject reworks what the first wrote instead of adding to it.
workers.compactHint: Off, a project can sit for three weeks and pick up where it was. On, its conversation is compacted like the personal one: Jenny then has in context what was written in the pages, not what was said. The transcript you read is untouched.
workers.compactRestart: This one takes effect from the next gateway start.
workers.savedRestart: Saved. Takes effect from the next start.

ssh.title: SSH
ssh.hint: Jenny can run commands on the machines you register here. Every host is added by hand: the agent can only name an alias you already declared, never an arbitrary address.
ssh.aliasHint: The only name Jenny uses for this host. It cannot be changed later.
ssh.authHint: A key is installed once on the server and can be revoked on its own, without touching the password you log in with. A password is more convenient and weaker: it is stored in config.json, not encrypted.
ssh.passwordPlaceholder: The password of that user on the server
ssh.passwordHint: Stays on the phone, inside config.json, like the Telegram token and the API keys.
ssh.passwordKeepBlank: Leave blank to keep the saved one.
ssh.passwordRequired: A password is required to save a host that authenticates with a password
ssh.fieldsRequired: Alias, host and user are required
ssh.credentialsLost: SSH access to {aliases} has to be set up again. The private key and the verified fingerprints deliberately live outside the workspace, so they are not in the backup and a restore cannot bring them back: regenerate the key, install the public one on the server and accept the fingerprint again.
ssh.noKeyYet: Generate the key, then install it on the server.
ssh.regenerateConfirm: Regenerate the key for {alias}? The one already installed on the server will stop working.
ssh.publicKeyHint: Paste this line into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server. The private key stays on the phone.
ssh.fingerprintIntro: Compare this fingerprint with the one on {alias} before accepting it. From now on Jenny will only talk to the machine that presents it.
ssh.fingerprintPasswordWarning: This host authenticates with a password: on the first command that password is handed to whichever machine presents this fingerprint. If it isn't yours, you gave it to them. With a password this step matters more than with a key, not less.
ssh.verifyCancelled: Fingerprint not accepted: the host stays unverified
ssh.changedWarning: {alias} is presenting a host key different from the one you accepted. It may be a reinstalled server, or someone sitting in the middle. Accept only if you know why it changed.
ssh.replaceConfirm: Replace the accepted fingerprint for {alias}? If you did not reinstall the server yourself, this is what an attack looks like.
ssh.deleteConfirm: Delete host {alias}? Its key and accepted fingerprint are deleted too.

battery.title: Background activity
battery.hint: Without a battery optimization exemption Android suspends Jenny while the screen is off: scheduled work, reminders and proactive checks arrive late or not at all.
battery.otaHint: A system update may have reset the battery optimization exemption. Without it, scheduled work and reminders start slipping again: worth turning it back on.
battery.granted: Exemption active: scheduled work, reminders and proactive checks keep running with the screen off.

keepAwakeCost.off: Best battery life, but scheduled work and reminders can slip by hours.
keepAwakeCost.turns: Wakes the processor for a turn, a cron job or an SSH command, then releases it: costs nothing at rest.
keepAwakeCost.always: Nothing ever slips, but it drains battery constantly: it makes sense for a phone on charge.

battery.keepAwakeHint: The exemption tells Android not to throttle Jenny; this choice decides whether Jenny keeps the processor awake herself. With the screen off the CPU suspends and timers stop firing.
battery.keepAwakeRestart: The new choice takes effect at the next Jenny restart: the service-lifetime lock is taken once, at startup.
battery.keepAwakeSaved: Saved — active from the next Jenny restart
battery.exactAlarmsHint: Android does not grant the exact alarm permission on its own: without it, it batches Jenny's wake-ups with other apps' and scheduled work, reminders and proactive checks arrive minutes — sometimes an hour — late.
battery.exactAlarmsRestart: Alarms already queued stay inexact even after the permission is granted: they go back to the exact minute from the next Jenny restart.
battery.exactAlarmsFailed: The permission screen could not be reached on this phone.
battery.diagUnavailable: Diagnostics are not available right now.
battery.gapsHint: An outage is a stretch of at least {minutes} minutes when Jenny was not running: reminders, scheduled jobs and proactive checks did not fire during that time.
battery.gapsEmpty: No outage recorded: Jenny stayed up.
battery.oemHint: The outages above are not a Jenny fault: the phone's battery manager shuts her down while the screen is off. No line of app code can prevent it — the restriction has to be lifted by hand, in the manufacturer's own settings.
battery.oemOpenFailed: No battery management screen could be reached on this phone.

fileHelp.agents:
The working conventions of this workspace: project preferences and the ways of doing things that keep coming back. Sections show up as you agree them with Jenny; a heading with nothing under it does not belong here.

Not here: facts about you (USER.md), personality and behaviour rules (SOUL.md), project context (memory/MEMORY.md), procedures with concrete steps and output formats (Skills, in the Apps section).
fileHelp.user:
What Jenny knows about you: identity, language, communication style, habits and interests. It fills in as she learns, so there is nothing to pre-write.

Not here: project context (memory/MEMORY.md), behaviour rules (SOUL.md), repeatable procedures (Skills). Nor the time, the timezone or where you are: the runtime measures those on its own every turn, while a copy written here has nobody to refresh it and is out of date the moment it is saved.
fileHelp.soul:
Who Jenny is and how she behaves: her character, the way she talks, what she does and what she will never do. Plus the standing rules you have given her — how to address you, what to steer clear of, where to tread carefully.

Dream, the consolidation pass that runs after conversations, is what maintains it: a correction you make in passing ends up here. You can read it and fix it, but you rarely need to write here by hand.

Not here: facts about you (USER.md), working conventions (AGENTS.md), repeatable procedures (Skills). Nor how the app itself behaves: what a tool accepts, what the sandbox refuses, where a limit sits — that is the same on every install, and the system prompt already tells her.
fileHelp.memory:
Long-term memory: what has to survive from one session to the next — project context, useful facts, notes worth keeping.

Dream, the consolidation pass that runs after conversations, is what maintains it. You can read it and correct it, but you rarely need to write here by hand.

Not here: facts about you (USER.md), working conventions (AGENTS.md), repeatable procedures (Skills).
fileHelp.heartbeat:
The recurring checks Jenny goes through on every heartbeat.

Write them under "## Active Tasks": that is the only section that gets read. When a task is done, delete it instead of leaving it there — a list of finished work is re-read on every beat.

Not here: one-off requests (just ask in chat) and repeatable procedures (Skills).
